questions.question: A girl goes to school at a speed of 9 km/hr. She comes back with a speed of 45 km/hr. Find her average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is constant, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y)

Here, x = 9 km/hr and y = 45 km/hr

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 9 × 45) ÷ (9 + 45)

⇒ Average Speed = 810 ÷ 54

⇒ Average Speed = 15 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 

 Home
 
 

 School
 
• 
 

 9 km/hr
 
• 
 

 45 km/hr
 Constant Distance = D

**Given:**

Speed to school (S₁) = 9 km/hr

Speed returning from school (S₂) = 45 km/hr

Let the distance between home and school be D km.

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D + D = 2D

⇒ Time taken to reach school (T₁) = D ÷ 9

⇒ Time taken to return home (T₂) = D ÷ 45

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 9) + (D ÷ 45)

⇒ Total Time = (5D + D) ÷ 45 = 6D ÷ 45 = 2D ÷ 15

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (2D ÷ 15)

⇒ Average Speed = (2D × 15) ÷ 2D

⇒ Average Speed = 15 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Times

If an object travels at speeds x and y for exactly equal amounts of time, the average speed is (x + y) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

If a body travels 3 equal parts of a journey at speeds x, y, and z respectively, the Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is (x + y). When they move in the same direction, it is |x − y|.

Speed Conversion Shortcut

To rapidly convert km/hr to m/s, simply multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. Conversely, to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
</p

questions.question: What is the HCF of 32, 28, and 24?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The HCF of given numbers is always a factor of the smallest difference between any two of the given numbers.

Given numbers: 32, 28, and 24

The difference between 28 and 24 is 4.

Since 4 perfectly divides 32, 28, and 24, the required HCF is 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers = 32, 28, and 24

**Method Used:**

Prime factorisation method: The Highest Common Factor (HCF) is determined by multiplying the lowest powers of all common prime factors among the numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorisation of 32 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁵

⇒ Prime factorisation of 28 = 2 × 2 × 7 = 2² × 7¹

⇒ Prime factorisation of 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2³ × 3¹

⇒ The common prime factor across all three numbers is 2.

⇒ The lowest power of the common prime factor 2 is 2².

⇒ HCF = 2² = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The LCM of two or more numbers is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors present in the prime factorisation of the numbers.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: a × b = HCF × LCM. Note: This rule does not hold true for three or more numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime numbers if they have no common factors other than 1, meaning their HCF is strictly equal to 1.
</p

questions.question: The average age of 39 students of a class is 27 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 28 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Teacher's Age = Old Average + (Total Members × Increase in Average)

⇒ Teacher's Age = 27 + (40 × 1)

⇒ Teacher's Age = 27 + 40 = 67

**∴ The correct answer is 67 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 39

Average age of 39 students = 27 years

New average age including the teacher = 28 years

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = Average × Number of Values

 
 39 Students : Avg = 27
 
 Teacher Added
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Total 40 Persons : New Avg = 28 (Avg increased by 1)
 Teacher's Age = 27 + (40 × 1) = 67

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 39 students = 39 × 27 = 1053 years

⇒ Total number of people including the teacher = 39 + 1 = 40

⇒ Total age of 40 people = 40 × 28 = 1120 years

⇒ Age of the teacher = Total age of 40 people − Total age of 39 students

⇒ Age of the teacher = 1120 − 1053 = 67 years

**∴ The correct answer is 67 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exclusion in Averages

When a member leaves a group, the value of the excluded member = Old Average − (Remaining Members × Change in Average).

Replacement in Averages

When a new member replaces an existing member, New Member's Value = Replaced Member's Value + (Total Members × Change in Average).

Combined Average

The combined average of two groups A and B is given by (N₁A₁ + N₂A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂), where N is the number of items and A is the average.
</p

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a mother and daughter is 42 years. After 5 years, the mother will be 3 times as old as her daughter at that time. Find the ratio of the daughter's present age to the mother's age after 4 years.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of their ages after 5 years = 42 + 5 + 5 = 52 years.

Ratio of Mother's age to Daughter's age after 5 years = 3 : 1 (Total 4 units).

⇒ 4 units = 52 ⇒ 1 unit = 13 years (Daughter's age after 5 years).

⇒ Daughter's present age = 13 − 5 = 8 years.

⇒ Mother's present age = 42 − 8 = 34 years.

Required ratio = 8 : (34 + 4) = 8 : 38 = 4 : 19.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 Present

 Daughter (D)
 M + D = 42

 
 
• 
 

 +5 Years

 
 
 After 5 Years
 Sum = 42 + 10 = 52
 Mother = 3x
 Daughter = 1x

Given,

Sum of present ages of mother and daughter = 42 years

Let the present age of the daughter be D and the mother be M.

⇒ M + D = 42 ⇒ M = 42 − D

After 5 years, the mother will be 3 times as old as her daughter.

⇒ (M + 5) = 3 × (D + 5)

Substitute M = 42 − D in the above equation:

⇒ (42 − D) + 5 = 3D + 15

⇒ 47 − D = 3D + 15

⇒ 4D = 32

⇒ D = 8 years (Daughter's present age)

Now, substitute D back into the first equation:

⇒ M = 42 − 8 = 34 years (Mother's present age)

Mother's age after 4 years = 34 + 4 = 38 years

Required ratio = Daughter's present age : Mother's age after 4 years

⇒ Ratio = 8 : 38 = 4 : 19

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 19.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference of Ages

The age difference between two individuals always remains constant over time. If a mother is 26 years older than her daughter today, she will remain exactly 26 years older forever. Only the sum and ratio of their ages change over time.

Shift in Sum of Ages

If the sum of present ages of 'n' people is S, then the sum of their ages after 't' years will be S + (n × t). Similarly, 't' years ago, it was S − (n × t).

Ratio Method in Ages

When multiple ratios for different time periods are given, you can equate the gap in ratio units to the actual gap in years to solve for the present age directly without algebra.
</p

questions.question: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 156 ^circ . How many sides does this polygon have?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any regular polygon, the sum of an interior angle and an exterior angle is always 180°.

Exterior Angle = 180° − 156° = 24°

Number of sides = 360° ÷ Exterior Angle = 360° ÷ 24° = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Interior angle of a regular polygon = 156°

**Formula Used:**

Interior angle = (n − 2) × 180° ÷ n

 

 

 

 

 156°
 24°
 Interior
 Exterior

**Calculations:**

⇒ 156° = (n − 2) × 180° ÷ n

⇒ 156n = 180n − 360

⇒ 180n − 156n = 360

⇒ 24n = 360

⇒ n = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of all exterior angles of any convex polygon is always exactly 360°, regardless of the number of sides.

Number of Diagonals

The total number of unique diagonals that can be drawn within an n-sided polygon is n(n − 3) ÷ 2.
</p

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 50 \% , 30 \% and 50 \% in three successive months, but increases by 65 \% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the initial price of the fuel to be 100 units.

Apply successive multiplying factors for the percentage changes:

Final Price = 100 × (1 − 0.50) × (1 − 0.30) × (1 − 0.50) × (1 + 0.65)

Final Price = 100 × 0.5 × 0.7 × 0.5 × 1.65 = 28.875

Total percentage decrease = 100 − 28.875 = 71.125% ≈ 71.13%

**∴ The correct answer is 71.13% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage decrease in 1st month = 50%

Percentage decrease in 2ⁿd month = 30%

Percentage decrease in 3rd month = 50%

Percentage increase in 4th month = 65%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100) ...

 
 
 

 
 

 −50%
 −30%
 −50%
 +65%

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 

 
 100
 
 
 50

 
 35

 
 17.5

 
 28.88

 

 

 Total Decrease = 71.13%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the original price of fuel be 100.

⇒ Price after 1st month = 100 × (100 − 50) ÷ 100 = 50

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd month = 50 × (100 − 30) ÷ 100 = 35

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 35 × (100 − 50) ÷ 100 = 17.5

⇒ Price after 4th month = 17.5 × (100 + 65) ÷ 100 = 17.5 × 1.65 = 28.875

⇒ Total decrease in price = Original Price − Final Price

⇒ Total decrease = 100 − 28.875 = 71.125

⇒ Percentage decrease = (71.125 ÷ 100) × 100% = 71.125%

⇒ Rounded off to two decimal places = 71.13%

**∴ The correct answer is 71.13% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive changes of A% and B%, the net effective percentage change is calculated as: Net Change = A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100. This formula can be chained for multiple months.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Using fractional multipliers simplifies complex calculations. For example, a decrease of 30% means the new value becomes (1 − 3/10) = 7/10 of the original value.

Base Independence

For pure percentage problems without any given numerical value, starting with an arbitrary base (commonly 100 or a multiple of the denominators) strictly preserves the ratio and the final percentage change.
</p

questions.question: The volume (in m³ ) of a cube, each edge of which is 45 m, is:

The volume of a cube is the cube of its side length (a³).

Since the side length is 45 m, the unit digit of its volume will be the unit digit of 5³, which is 5.

 a = 45 m

**Calculations:**

Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a cube with side length 'a' is the sum of the areas of its 6 square faces, given by the formula 6a².

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

Diagonal of a Cube

questions.question: If 20% of 10% of 3/4 of a number is 882, find the number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given percentages to their fractional equivalents directly.

20% = 1/5 and 10% = 1/10

Combined multiplying factor = 1/5 × 1/10 × 3/4 = 3/200

If 3 parts → 882, then 1 part → 294

Total value (200 parts) = 294 × 200 = 58800

**∴ The correct answer is 58800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

20% of 10% of 3/4 of a number is 882.

 
 N 
• × 3/4 3N/4 
• 10% 3N/40 
• 20% 882 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required number be N.

⇒ 20% of 10% of 3/4 of N = 882

⇒ (20/100) × (10/100) × (3/4) × N = 882

⇒ (1/5) × (1/10) × (3/4) × N = 882

⇒ (3/200) × N = 882

⇒ N = 882 × (200/3)

⇒ N = 294 × 200

⇒ N = 58800

**∴ The correct answer is 58800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions speeds up calculations. Remember standard values: 10% = 1/10, 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4, and 50% = 1/2.

BODMAS Rule in Simplification

Always solve the 'of' operator before division and multiplication operations. In algebraic representations, 'of' directly translates to multiplication (×).

Successive Operations

When multiple percentages or fractions are applied sequentially on the same base, multiply their fractional equivalents to find the overall net multiplying factor.

questions.question: A dealer incurs a loss of 5% if he sells an article for ₹1805. At what price must he sell the article so as to gain 5% on that article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the unitary method, we can find the new selling price directly from the ratio of percentages.

Given SP₁ corresponds to a 5% loss (95% of CP).

Target SP₂ corresponds to a 5% gain (105% of CP).

Target SP₂ = SP₁ × (105 ÷ 95)

Target SP₂ = 1805 × (21 ÷ 19) = 95 × 21 = 1995

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1995.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹1805

Loss percentage = 5%

Target Profit percentage = 5%

 
 CP (100%)
 ₹1900
 
 
 SP₁ (95%)
 ₹1805
 
 
 SP₂ (105%)
 ₹?
 
 

 

 −5%
 
 

 

 +5%

 Profit & Loss Flow

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)]

New Selling Price (SP₂) = CP × [(100 + Profit%) ÷ 100]

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = 1805 × [100 ÷ (100 − 5)]

⇒ CP = 1805 × (100 ÷ 95)

⇒ CP = 19 × 100 = ₹1900

⇒ To gain 5%, SP₂ = 1900 × [(100 + 5) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP₂ = 1900 × (105 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP₂ = 19 × 105 = 1995

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1995.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

CP is considered as the base value (100%). All standard profit and loss calculations are measured against the CP.

Marked Price (MP)

MP is the catalog price. Discounts are always evaluated on the Marked Price: SP = MP × [(100 − Discount%) ÷ 100].

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer uses a false weight, Profit% = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.

questions.question: A dealer allowed a 65% discount on an article and was still able to manage an 82% profit. Find the ratio of the cost price to the listed price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can use the direct ratio relation between Cost Price and Marked Price (Listed Price):

CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%)

⇒ CP : MP = (100 − 65) : (100 + 82)

⇒ CP : MP = 35 : 182

⇒ CP : MP = 5 : 26 (Dividing by 7)

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount percentage (D%) = 65%

Profit percentage (P%) = 82%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price / Marked Price = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

 
 CP
 
 
 SP
 
 
 MP

 

 

 +82% Profit

 

 

 -65% Discount

 Ratio CP : MP = (100 − 65) : (100 + 82)
 CP : MP = 35 : 182 = 5 : 26

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Listed Price (MP) be 100 units.

⇒ SP = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 100 − 65 = 35 units

⇒ Profit = 82%

⇒ SP = CP × (100 + 82) / 100

⇒ 35 = CP × 182 / 100

⇒ CP = 3500 / 182

Now, finding the ratio of CP to MP:

⇒ Ratio = (3500 / 182) / 100

⇒ Ratio = 35 / 182

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by 7:

⇒ Ratio = 5 / 26

⇒ CP : MP = 5 : 26

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct CP & MP Relation

The formula CP/MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%) is the fastest way to solve questions where profit and discount percentages are given and actual prices are not required.

Marked Price (MP) vs Cost Price (CP)

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (Listed Price) to find the Selling Price. Profit or Loss is always calculated over the Cost Price.

Successive Discount

When two discounts a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is calculated using the formula: (a + b − ab/100)%.

questions.question: The average speed of a car running at 70 { km/hr} for 1 { hour} and ‘ p ’ {km/hr} for 1(1)/(2) { hours} is 52 { km/hr} . Find the value of p.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can solve this quickly using the weighted average method based on the time ratio.

Ratio of times = 1 hr : 1.5 hr = 2 : 3

Weighted Average Speed = (Speed₁ × Ratio₁ + Speed₂ × Ratio₂) ÷ (Ratio₁ + Ratio₂)

⇒ (70 × 2 + p × 3) ÷ (2 + 3) = 52

⇒ 140 + 3p = 260 ⇒ 3p = 120 ⇒ p = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed for first part (v₁) = 70 km/hr

Time for first part (t₁) = 1 hr

Speed for second part (v₂) = p km/hr

Time for second part (t₂) = 1.5 hr

Overall Average Speed = 52 km/hr

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 v₁ = 70 km/hr
 t₁ = 1 hr
 
 v₂ = p km/hr
 t₂ = 1.5 hr

 

 Total Avg Speed = 52 km/hr

 

 Total Time = 2.5 hr | Total Dist = (70 + 1.5p) km

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = (v₁ × t₁) + (v₂ × t₂)

Total Time = t₁ + t₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = (70 × 1) + (p × 1.5) = (70 + 1.5p) km

⇒ Total Time = 1 + 1.5 = 2.5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = (70 + 1.5p) ÷ 2.5 = 52

⇒ 70 + 1.5p = 52 × 2.5

⇒ 70 + 1.5p = 130

⇒ 1.5p = 130 − 70

⇒ 1.5p = 60

⇒ p = 60 ÷ 1.5

⇒ p = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General Formula)

Average speed is always equal to the Total Distance covered divided by the Total Time taken. This is primarily used when distances or times for different segments are unequal.

Average Speed (Equal Distance Concept)

If an object covers two equal parts of a journey at speeds x and y, the average speed can be directly calculated using the formula: Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Concept)

When a person travels at two different speeds x and y for an exact same duration of time, the average speed becomes the simple arithmetic mean of the two speeds: Average Speed = (x + y) ÷ 2.
</p

questions.question: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 12 days, B and C together can do it in 15 days, and C and A together can finish it in 20 days. Find the ratio of the number of days taken by B and C to complete the work individually.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units.

Efficiencies: A+B = 5, B+C = 4, C+A = 3.

Total combined efficiency = 2(A+B+C) = 12 ⇒ A+B+C = 6.

Efficiency of B = 6 − 3 = 3, Efficiency of C = 6 − 5 = 1.

Time ratio is inversely proportional to efficiency ratio ⇒ Time B : Time C = 1 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 12 days

Time taken by B and C together = 15 days

Time taken by C and A together = 20 days

**Method Used:**

LCM Method (Total Work = LCM of Days)

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B
 12
 60
 5
 
 

 B + C
 15
 4
 
 

 C + A
 20
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Adding all efficiencies: 2(A + B + C) = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12

⇒ Combined efficiency of A + B + C = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = (A + B + C) − (C + A) = 6 − 3 = 3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = (A + B + C) − (A + B) = 6 − 5 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ B's efficiency = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 days

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ C's efficiency = 60 ÷ 1 = 60 days

⇒ Ratio of number of days taken by B and C individually = 20 : 60 = 1 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 1:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency vs Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If A and B take time in ratio x : y, their efficiency ratio will be y : x.

Pipes and Cisterns

Follows the exact same logic as Time and Work. A filling pipe has positive efficiency while a leaking or emptying pipe has negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of work done. If people work for the same number of days, wages are divided in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.
</p

questions.question: Find the sum of the squares of x and y, given that the number 83y547x is divisible by 72.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisible by 72 ⇒ divisible by 8 and 9

47x divisible by 8 ⇒ x = 2

Sum = 29 + y divisible by 9 ⇒ y = 7

x² + y² = 4 + 49

**∴ Answer = 53**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

83y547x is divisible by 72

**Concept Used:**

Divisibility rule of 72 ⇒ divisible by 8 and 9

**Calculation:**

⇒ Last three digits = 47x

⇒ 470 + x divisible by 8

⇒ 470 leaves remainder 6 ⇒ x = 2

⇒ Sum of digits = 8 + 3 + y + 5 + 4 + 7 + 2

⇒ = 29 + y

⇒ 29 + y divisible by 9 ⇒ y = 7

⇒ x² + y² = 2² + 7²

⇒ = 4 + 49

⇒ = 53

**∴ The correct answer is 53.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 8

Last three digits must be divisible by 8

Divisibility by 9

Sum of digits divisible by 9

Combined Rule

72 = 8 × 9, so both conditions must hold

questions.question: The average of 13 numbers is 92. If the first 7 numbers are 30, 32, 46, 81, 110, 73 and 20, then what will be the average of the remaining numbers?

⇒ Sum of remaining numbers = 1196 − 392 = 804

⇒ Average = 804 ÷ 6

Target value = 1/30

 Percentage Comparison

questions.question: If 2x + 3y = 8 and 4x² + 9y² = 32 , find the value of 8x³ + 27y³ .
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

(2x + 3y)² = 4x² + 9y² + 12xy

⇒ 64 = 32 + 12xy ⇒ 12xy = 32 ⇒ xy = 8/3

Use identity:

(2x)³ + (3y)³ = (2x + 3y)³ − 3(2x)(3y)(2x + 3y)

= 8³ − 3×(6xy)×8

= 512 − 144xy

= 512 − 144×(8/3) = 512 − 384 = 128

**∴ Answer = 128**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

2x + 3y = 8

4x² + 9y² = 32

**Formula used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let a = 2x, b = 3y

⇒ (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ 8² = 32 + 2ab

⇒ 64 = 32 + 2ab

⇒ 2ab = 32 ⇒ ab = 16

⇒ a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b)

⇒ = 8³ − 3×16×8

⇒ = 512 − 384 = 128

**∴ The correct answer is 128.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
